messages:
amanda: Quick heads-up — I pushed a prototype dashboard for keying observability: https://grafana.redwood/r/UXkeying123
sanjay: Nice. What exactly are we measuring there?
amanda: Top-level: 'prefix_coverage' (pct of requests that produce any cache key), 'hit_rate' by model/route/customer, and 'tokens_saved' aggregated by day. Early 7d rollup: overall coverage ~18%, but model=chat-small is ~42%. Tokens_saved ~1.4M tokens/day estimate.
leah: Can you slice tokens_saved by route + customer? PMs keep asking per-tenant econs.
amanda: Yep — panels: per-model hit_rate, per-route hit_rate, per-customer tokens_saved, latency_ms delta (hit vs miss), key_entropy histogram, and a rolling 'kv_warmup_success' rate.
marc: FYI — kernel changes in last deploy looked like they affected long-context key formation. I saw miss-rate bumps for longseqs.
ops-bot: deploy 1751234 completed to prod (serving/kernels) :rocket:
amanda: After that deploy we saw model=x-longctx miss-rate +7pp on top routes and tail-latency +12ms. Putting that into the panel.
sanjay: Can you add a metric 'kv_warmup_success_rate' = fraction of warmup ops that actually primed the KV store before first real request? That was flaky in canary.
leah: Also add 'key_stability_v2' showing fraction of keys that mutate across tiny prompt edits (truncation/whitespace differences). We suspect tokenization changes affect stability.
amanda: Draft query I used for the per-customer table (SQL snippet):
```sql
SELECT route, customer, model,
  count(*) as requests,
  sum(is_cache_hit) as hits,
  round(sum(tokens_saved)/1000) as k_tokens_saved
FROM prefix_cache_events
WHERE ts > now() - interval '7 days'
GROUP BY 1,2,3
ORDER BY k_tokens_saved DESC
```
marc: Nice. Add one more panel: 'hit_yield_per_kernel' so we can correlate kernel selection with hit yield. Kernel team needs to see economics impact.
amanda: Wired kernel tags into the query. Early signal: kernels using fused-attn show ~3% lower hit_yield for longctx workloads — could be key normalization differences around tokenization boundary. Needs repro.
sanjay: I'll triage: reproduce with the perf harness and trace id 0x7f3a from last canary. If kernel changes cause key diffs, that explains the spike.
leah: I'll own promoting the dashboard to prod if we agree on panels + alerts.
amanda: Proposed alerts: 
- hit_rate drop >5 percentage points sustained for 30m for top 10 routes
- tokens_saved drop >20% over 1h for prod pool
- kv_warmup_success_rate < 80% on any dedicated pool for 15m
These should auto-create a ticket and tag oncall.
marc: Add runbook link: https://confluence.redwood/obs/keying-playbook (contains triage steps, how to run local keyizer, and regression checklist)
ops-bot: incident auto-create enabled for alert prefix-hit-drop
sanjay: Tagging kernel-team and routing-team; I'll follow up with a small repro. @kernel-team please check tokenization micro-changes in the fused-attn path.
leah: Can we add a cheap CDF viz for key entropy per-route so product can see when a single key is dominating token-saved?
amanda: Done — entropy panel + top-20 keys per-customer. Found one route where top key accounts for 62% of saved tokens (skew).
marc: Action items: reproduce kernel diff locally (sanjay), add kv-warmup metric to telemetry ingest (amanda), build per-customer tokens_saved alert (leah).
ops-bot: calendar invite created: Prefix Observability sync — tomorrow 09:00 PT
sanjay: Meeting invite accepted, I'll bring perf traces.
amanda: TL;DR — new observability panels pushed, initial signals show kernel-related hit-yield shifts on long-context flows; next steps: add kv warmup metric, per-customer tokens_saved slices, alerting + runbook. :white_check_mark:
leah: Thanks everyone — will send the prod dashboard link once panels are promoted.
marc: One more note: when we run the regression harness, include the greedy vs sampling prompt variations; they produce different key shapes.
amanda: Good call. I added both sampling modes to the comparison matrix.
sanjay: I'll hand off a short reproducible patch to kernel team by EOD if we confirm key diffs.
leah: Sounds good. Closing the loop here. :thumbsup:
